problem: Existing language maps for navigation store CLIP vectors explicitly in 2D grids or topological graph nodes, which blows up memory in large environments (dense grids) or gives only coarse resolution (sparse nodes) and cannot guide fine-grained goal reaching or unobserved goals.
motivation: Robots need to follow language queries in large indoor/outdoor spaces, including small objects and goals that no node directly observed. Coarse maps miss small objects, while dense maps are too memory-heavy. A continuous field can infer language features at unvisited poses and provide gradients for fine refinement.
key_idea: Learn a NeRF-style MLP mapping camera pose to a CLIP embedding (with vMF uncertainty) and use it with a sparse pose-only graph for coarse A* search followed by gradient-based pose optimization toward the query embedding.
insight: Storing only node poses and generating embeddings on demand gives about 0.057 GB versus 56 GB for a dense grid at comparable success rates. The coarse stage gets 42-67% success, and the gradient refinement cuts goal distance by about 50% (paper's text claim), showing the continuous field carries fine-grained information nodes cannot. The node-sampling ablation shows the uncertainty (kappa) term chiefly lifts SR/SPL and adding semantic sensitivity gives the lowest GDist (4.05).
method: Implicit language map: NeRF-style MLP (positional encoding, skip connections) maps pose x=[t,q]∈R^7 to a 512-d CLIP embedding, trained on pose-image pairs from RGB only
Sparse topological graph: nodes store only poses, embeddings are generated on demand by F_Θ, avoiding explicit vector storage

Bayesian vMF head: network outputs mean direction μ and concentration κ, trained with negative log-posterior with a Gamma prior on κ (α=2, β=0.5) to handle noisy multi-object CLIP features and generalize to unseen poses
Graph sampling: score = w1·view coverage (quaternion dissimilarity over two-hop neighbours) + w2·uncertainty (κ) + w3·semantic sensitivity (gradient norm of F_Θ wrt pose); keep top nodes (w=1,1,0.5)
Coarse planning: encode query with CLIP, choose node with highest cosine similarity, A* on the sampled graph
Fine path generation: sample candidate poses near the coarse pose, pick x_best, then Adam-optimize δx to maximize similarity minus λ_dist·distance to x_best (λ=5) to avoid local minima

setting.backbone: NeRF-style MLP (positional encoding + skip) predicting CLIP embedding + vMF concentration; CLIP for text/image features (trained per scene)
setting.training_data: Per-scene self-collected pose-image pairs: 5M in Isaac Sim City Tower scene; 10k-20k per floor in the real building; CLIP features as targets
setting.observation: RGB images with camera poses during mapping (map built from pose-image pairs); poses on the graph at test time
setting.action_space: Graph node search (A*) followed by continuous pose refinement to a goal pose
setting.simulator: NVIDIA Isaac Sim (City Tower Demo pack, 1.6 km x 1.8 km)
setting.privileged: Pre-collected pose-image data from extensive exploration and known camera poses (map is built beforehand); static environment

numbers.extra: Memory 0.057 GB; time 0.8041 s; Easy = objects ≥1 m^3; success within 20 m of object center; SR from top 1% predictions; SR/SPL given as proportions
Hard = objects <1 m^3; memory 0.057 GB; time 0.8041 s

numbers_note: Simulation benchmark is the authors' own Isaac Sim setup, not a standard benchmark; SR/SPL are proportions as printed.
results: With the same memory (~0.057 GB), LAMP gets Easy SR 0.67 / Hard SR 0.42 versus sparse node-based 0.41 / 0.21 and sparse grid 0.08 / 0.0. Dense grid (56.34 GB) and dense node (3.962 GB) reach comparable SR but LAMP has lower GDist than the dense node method on Easy (6.36 vs 7.51) and uses far less memory. In the real building, equal success (90%) to an explicit baseline but GDist 1.89 vs 5.19 m.
limitations: Depends on VLM/CLIP accuracy; confusable or weak-appearance targets cause wrong node selection
Slower per query than explicit maps (0.80 s vs 0.0001-0.34 s sim; 3.84 s vs 1.82 s real) and requires per-scene training on extensive pre-collected pose-image data with a static map
Evaluation is on a custom simulator benchmark and a single small real-world trial; dense baselines still beat LAMP on hard-case SR/GDist
